why: Madhav, 24 Nov 2026: 'do you think that we can come up with some refined question set ... based on what we have done here in these audits for the next audit', then 'Yes please, draft it and save it for the next audits and tests'. Built from what broke in the 23 Nov audit, the 24 Nov stress test and the open list (flags 226-249).
for: stress test run 2 (flag 250, about 4 Dec): blocks C, D and E, asked at stand-in moments with scripts/india_stress_words.py
the random audit of 29 Dec 2026: every core block, plus at least 5 fresh questions
any later audit: the core set unchanged, fresh questions new each time
rules: CORE questions never change, so each audit compares with the last (the no-drop rule of the stress test, applied to audits). A core question may be added, never edited or dropped; a changed question gets a new id.

FRESH questions are new each audit: at least 5, written that week by an agent that does not build Ananta, and not shown to the builder before the run. They keep Ananta from being tuned to the bank. The fresh pool below is examples, not a list to reuse.

Every answer is graded three ways: (1) code checks every number and date it carries against the truth sheet built from the live system at the moment of asking; (2) a blind grader judges the rest (the S1-S5 grades of 23 Nov); (3) Madhav reads 10 answers himself, drawn at random, and marks each right, partly or wrong. His read is the one grader that is not a model.
A 'carry' line is what a right answer must contain, in any words; it is checked against the truth sheet, not by matching words (the stress test's word lists missed honest phrasings twice).
A 'never' line is a hard fail whatever else is right.
Blocks marked live_only are asked only once the live path exists (flag 239); before that they are skipped and said so.
never_anywhere: contradicts the clock, the session state or the options line's ledger (livesession.check)
gives a figure that is not in the facts
promises a result, a recovery or a return
tells Madhav to put real money in, or act with it, now
pastes raw error text (HTTP 400, TokenException, a traceback)
names crypto items in an India answer while crypto is on hold

pass_marks.carry: at least 90% of the core questions' carry lines right
pass_marks.never: no never-line broken in any answer
pass_marks.grader: at least 80% of answers pass the blind grader
pass_marks.madhav: at least 8 of his 10 marked right or partly, none wrong in a way that would have cost money
pass_marks.no_drop: no core block scores below its own result at the previous audit
